lessons.title: Solving two equations of first degree in two variables Graphically and Algebraically

objectives.label: Solutions of two-variable equation
objectives.description: Find ordered-pair solutions of a first-degree equation in two variables by writing it in the form y = ... or x = ... and substituting values, and represent its solution set as a straight line.

objectives.label: Solve simultaneous equations graphically
objectives.description: Solve two first-degree equations in two variables graphically by drawing both lines and reading the solution set from the intersection point, identifying when the lines are parallel or coincide.

objectives.label: Solve simultaneous equations algebraically
objectives.description: Solve two first-degree equations in two variables algebraically by substitution or by omitting (eliminating) one variable, and state the number of solutions.

objectives.label: Apply simultaneous equations
objectives.description: Form and solve a pair of first-degree equations in two variables from a given solution or word problem to find unknown coefficients or numbers.

entries.text: A shaded rectangle with the vertical side labelled Y cm and the horizontal side labelled X cm.

A.why: The rectangle with sides X and Y illustrates the perimeter activity that leads to x + y = 15.

B.why: Rectangle with sides X and Y illustrates the perimeter activity that introduces the equation.

entries.text: The equation x + y = 15 is called the equation of first degree in two variables. $x+y=15$

A.why: Defines the first-degree equation in two variables, the starting point for finding its solutions.

B.why: Names x + y = 15 as a first-degree equation in two variables.

entries.text: Solving this equation means finding an ordered pair of real numbers that satisfies the equation.

A.why: States that solving means finding an ordered pair satisfying the equation.

B.why: Defines solving the equation as finding an ordered pair satisfying it.

entries.text: If x ∈ R then the substitution set is R × R, so the equation of the first degree has infinitely many solutions, each an ordered pair (x, y) whose first projection is x and second projection is y. $R\times R$

A.why: Says the equation has infinitely many ordered-pair solutions in R × R.

B.why: States that the equation has infinitely many ordered-pair solutions in R×R.

entries.text: Coordinate grid with x`x and y`y axes, line L through (0,-1) and (2,3), arrowheads at both ends, labelled L. Axis ticks -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 and y 1, 2, 3, -1. Values read from the figure; verify.

A.why: The line L is the straight-line graph of the solution set of 2x - y = 1.

B.why: Line L graphs the solution set of a two-variable equation as a straight line.

entries.text: Coordinate grid with X`X and YY` axes; red line L1 through (0,-3) and (2,1) and (4,5); blue line L2 through (0,2), (2,1), (4,0), sloping down; they intersect at (2,1) with dashed guide lines to the axes. Labels L1, L2. Values read from the figure; verify.

A.why: Two lines L1 and L2 meeting at (2,1) show the graphical solution of the pair.

B.why: Two lines intersecting at (2,1) show reading the solution from the intersection point.

entries.text: Graph on a grid with axes X'X, Y'Y, two parallel red lines L1 and L2 sloping downward. Y axis marked 1–4 upward and -1, -2 downward; X axis marked -2, -1, 1, 2. L1 passes (0,4) and (2,-2); L2 passes through (0,3/2) and (1,-3/2). Points read from figure; verify.

A.why: Parallel lines illustrate the graphical case with no common point.

B.why: Parallel lines L1 and L2 show the graphical case with no solution.

entries.text: Graph with axes x'x, y'y and one red line labelled L1 and L2 (coincident), sloping downward, passing through (0,3) and (2,0) with blue points marked, and also through about (4,-3). Y axis marked 1–8, -1 to -3; X axis -3 to 4. Read from figure; verify.

A.why: Coincident lines illustrate the graphical case with infinitely many solutions.

B.why: Coincident lines L1 and L2 illustrate the graphical case with infinitely many solutions.

lessons.title: Solving an equation of second degree in one unknown Graphically and Algebraically

objectives.label: Solve graphically
objectives.description: Draw the graph of a quadratic function f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c in a given interval and read the solution set of the equation from the x-coordinates of the points where the curve meets the x-axis.

objectives.label: Solve by factorising or completing square
objectives.description: Solve a quadratic equation by factorizing the left side or by completing the square, and write the solution set.

objectives.label: Use the general rule (quadratic formula)
objectives.description: Solve a quadratic equation algebraically using the general rule (quadratic formula), rounding the solutions, and reject a solution that does not fit a real-life context.

entries.text: Draw the curve of the function f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c where a ≠ 0. $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c, a\neq 0$

A.why: The method for drawing the curve of a quadratic function is the graphical solution procedure.

B.why: It states the first step of the graphical method: draw the curve of f(x)=ax^2+bx+c.

entries.text: Ordered pairs of f: x values and y = f(x) x, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, -1 / y = f(x), 8, 3, 0, -1, 0, 3, 8

A.why: The table of ordered pairs is used to draw the curve of f and find where it meets the x-axis.

B.why: The ordered pairs of f are the table used to draw the curve in the graphical method.

entries.text: Graph on coordinate plane (axes x`x, y`y) of a parabola opening upward, passing through (-1,8), (0,3), (1,0), minimum at about (2,-1), (3,0), rising on right. Axis ticks from -4 to 4 on x, up to 8 on y.

A.why: The parabola crosses the x-axis at x=1 and x=3, giving the solutions graphically.

B.why: The parabola of f(x)=x^2-4x+3 meets the x-axis at 1 and 3, giving the graphical solution.

lessons.title: Solving two equations in two variables, one of them is of the first degree and the other is of the second degree

objectives.label: Solve by substitution
objectives.description: Solve algebraically two equations in two variables, one of the first degree and one of the second degree, by substitution and state the solution set.

objectives.label: Solve rectangle dimension problems
objectives.description: Solve a word problem about a rectangle's perimeter and area by forming one first-degree and one second-degree equation and finding its two dimensions.

entries.text: You know that 2x - y = 3 is an equation of the first degree in two variables while x^2 + y = 5 and xy = 2 are equations of the second degree in two variables. Why?

A.why: It recalls the known degree of equations in two variables, which the lesson assumes rather than teaches.

B.why: It recalls how to tell first-degree from second-degree equations, which the lesson assumes and doesn't teach.
